messages.author: 3a775dfa0a96bf95
messages.subject: Issues with idata.frame
parts:
I really like the idea of idata.frame.  I wonder if the following things are the way they are because of the way R's class system works, or if they're just on the To Be Done queue:

In the following,

    test <- idata.frame(data.frame(a=floor((1:5)/2),b=1:5))

* idata.frame's don't print like a data frame.  Is there any problem with something simple like:
      print.idf <- function(x) {cat('IDF ',length(x$`_rows`),'/',nrow(x$`_data`),'\n',sep=''); print(as.data.frame(x))}
* "data.frame" is not among the classes of an idata.frame
* I can't add new columns.  I assume this is intentional/desirable, but then shouldn't test$c <- 99 give an error instead of adding a 'c' attribute to the environment?
* Many operations don't sem to work:
      rbind(test,test)
               -- fix: rbind.idf <- function(...,deparse.level = 1) idata.frame(do.call(rbind,lapply(list(...),as.data.frame)))
      subset(test,b==3)     # can't find variable 'b' 
               -- fix is subset.idf <- subset.data.frame 
      subset(test, test$b==3 )   # returns peculiar object; as.data.frame(...) => NULL
               -- above fix works
      dlply(test,.(a),subset,b==max(b))    # works with the above fix
               -- above fix works
      ddply(test,.(a),subset,b==max(b))
               -- still doesn't work, despite rbind.idf definition
      do.call(rbind,dlply(test,.(a),subset,b==max(b))) -- but this works

Adding 'data.frame' to the classes of test doesn't seem to fix the subset problem and it screws up printing -- I don't understand R's method dispatching mechanism :-(

I'm using plyr 1.5.2 on R 2.13.0 64-bit, Windows.
